findings.evidence: Roadmap grep: `ContourIntegration/README.md:32-33` says a piecewise-`C¹` curve is continuous and `C¹` on each piece of a finite partition; PR grep: lines 60-63 require only `ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)` plus pointwise differentiability and `ContinuousAt (deriv γ)` on `Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ p`, with no one-sided derivative limit or `ContDiffOn` condition at breakpoints.
findings.fix: Define the predicate using an actual finite partition and require `ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ` (or equivalent within-derivative plus continuous extension data) on each closed subinterval/piece, allowing corners only between pieces.
findings.issue: `IsPiecewiseC1On` only asks for `DifferentiableAt` and `ContinuousAt (deriv γ)` away from the finite set, so a cusp with unbounded derivative at a breakpoint, e.g. `γ t = sqrt |t|` at `0`, satisfies the predicate on `[-1,1]` although it is not C¹ on either closed partition piece adjacent to `0`.

summary: The predicate is still weaker than the roadmap's piecewise-C¹ object: it accepts curves with finite nondifferentiability points but no C¹ extension on the adjacent partition pieces.
